title: HfO2/SiO2 21-layer stack with ±8% quarter-wave bounded optimization
scientific_hypothesis: Constraining thickness optimization bounds to ±8% around deterministic quarter-wave targets at 267.5 nm center wavelength will enable the solver to rapidly converge on physically dominant standing-wave modes, improving target score over the previous 0.5x-1.5x broad bounds that allowed excessive deviation from interference conditions.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stack at central passband wavelength with tight bounded perturbation for bandwidth tuning while preserving constructive interference in UV passband and destructive interference in visible/NIR blocking bands.
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | Fused silica (21 finite layers, alternating HfO2/SiO2 starting and ending with HfO2)
design_variables: Layer thicknesses with ±8% bounds around quarter-wave targets at 267.5 nm
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness tolerance ±8% reflects realistic deposition control
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory: optical thickness n*d = lambda_center/4 creates constructive interference at design wavelength
Standing-wave mode locking through tight bound initialization
expected_advantages: Faster convergence to physically meaningful solutions
Reduced search space eliminates non-physical thickness combinations
Preserves interference conditions that produced 0.5036 baseline score
known_risks: ±8% bounds may be too restrictive if optimal design requires larger deviations
HfO2 absorption at 255 nm may limit maximum achievable UV transmission
21-layer count may be insufficient for broad visible/NIR blocking
execution_request_english: Optimize a 21-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack on fused silica substrate under normal incidence. Initialize all layer thicknesses at quarter-wave optical thickness for 267.5 nm center wavelength (HfO2: n≈2.05 at 267.5 nm gives ~32.7 nm physical thickness; SiO2: n≈1.48 at 267.5 nm gives ~45.2 nm physical thickness). Apply optimization bounds of ±8% around these quarter-wave targets for each layer. Stack sequence: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | Fused silica. Optimize layer thicknesses to maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm band while minimizing mean transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm bands. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 255–280 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Transmittance in 300–700 nm; Transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: Maximum 30 layers; No metal layers; Only conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Changed from route_06's 0.5x-1.5x broad thickness bounds to ±8% bounds around deterministic quarter-wave targets at 267.5 nm center wavelength. This addresses the insight directive to reinitialize with quarter-wave thickness targets and restrict optimizer bounds to force rapid locking onto physically dominant standing-wave modes before permitting broader perturbations.
